card.lives_in: Woodley, near Reading, South East England
card.occupation: Associate structural engineer at a mid-sized engineering consultancy in central Reading, working mainly on commercial and residential refurbishment schemes
card.education_detail: BSc in Civil Engineering from the University of Natal in Durban, completed in 1999. Chartered Engineer (CEng) and Member of the Institution of Structural Engineers since 2008, after qualifying through the UK route.
card.household: Lives alone in a three-bedroom 1970s semi in Woodley that he kept after his divorce four years ago. His daughter, 15, lives with her mum in Earley and stays with him every other weekend and one evening a week. The spare room is mostly her room.
card.cultural_background: Born and raised in Durban, South Africa, in an English-speaking white family. His parents became Bahá'ís in the 1970s and brought him up in the faith. He still describes himself as Bahá'í and goes to the occasional local gathering, particularly around Naw-Rúz in March. He keeps it low-key and practical rather than devout, and doesn't drink, which he puts down partly to upbringing and partly to habit. He came to the UK at 24 on a work visa, intending to stay two years, and is now a British citizen. His parents are still in Durban and his younger sister is in Perth, Australia.
card.professional_persona: Steady and reliable, the engineer people go to when they want a straight answer on whether a beam will take the load. He works long hours, usually 50 to 55 a week, mostly because project deadlines stack up and he'd rather finish things than leave them hanging. He's not interested in office politics or networking events. He gets on fine with the team but doesn't socialise much beyond the odd leaving do. He prefers proven methods and gets mildly irritated by new software rollouts that change things for the sake of it.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong rugby follower who supports the Springboks and watches every test, usually alone at home with the TV loud. He watches Premiership rugby casually too. He cycles on his own on weekend mornings, the same few loops out towards Wargrave and Henley, and does a gym session twice a week before work at a budget gym near the office.
card.arts_persona: Not much of one. He listens to the same rock he liked in his twenties: Bon Jovi, Dire Straits, a bit of Johnny Clegg from home. He watches crime dramas and documentaries about engineering or the war. He hasn't been to a gallery or theatre in years, apart from his daughter's school productions, which he attends without fail.
card.travel_persona: He goes back to Durban roughly every 18 months to see his parents, usually over Christmas or the Easter break. Beyond that he takes one week abroad a year, normally the Algarve or Crete, at the same type of hotel. He doesn't see the point of city breaks and isn't drawn to anywhere he hasn't been.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, dependable cooking: a small rotation of stir-fries, chicken and rice, pasta bake and steak. He braais on a gas barbecue in the garden whenever the weather allows, including in October, and buys boerewors from a South African shop online. He has a weakness for rusks with his morning coffee and makes his own biltong in a homemade drying box in the garage.
hobbies_and_interests: Solo road cycling on weekend mornings
Odd jobs and DIY around the house
Keeping the garden tidy, mainly the lawn
skills: Structural calculations and design using standard industry software
Reviewing contractor drawings and spotting problems quickly
Staying calm when site issues go wrong
card.career_goals: No grand ambitions. He'd accept a director-level role if it were offered, but won't chase it. His main aim is to keep the work steady, pay off the mortgage in about eight years, help his daughter through university, and maybe cut down to four days a week in his mid-fifties.
card.voice: A South African accent softened by 24 years in Berkshire. Flat vowels still come through on some words, and he occasionally says 'ja' instead of 'yeah' without noticing. He speaks at a measured pace, in fairly short sentences, and gets to the point. He uses 'er' when thinking and the odd 'sort of' as a hedge. He calls the evening meal 'dinner'. He isn't bothered by silence on a call; he'll wait for the next question rather than fill the gap. When he's unsure what's being asked he'll say 'sorry, what was that?' rather than guess.
card.typing: Proper capitals and full stops, apostrophes correct, no abbreviations or emojis. Answers are short and literal, often one sentence, and he rarely adds extra detail unless a field explicitly asks him to explain.
card.with_strangers: Polite, reserved and a bit dry. He answers what he's asked without volunteering much and doesn't do much small talk, but he isn't cold. He'll crack a deadpan joke now and then. Some people read him as unbothered or hard to read at first.
small_things: The traffic on the A329(M) in the mornings
Whether the Springboks squad is any good this year
A loop he cycled at the weekend
Needing to sort out the guttering
deeper_things: The divorce was mostly about him working too much and not talking enough, and he accepts some of that
He worries a little about his parents getting older so far away
He sometimes wonders whether he should have gone back to South Africa, but doesn't think he'd fit there now either
His faith is more a habit and a link to his parents than something he thinks hard about
Weekends without his daughter can feel very quiet
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop camera slightly below eye level, so the view is a little upward. Lighting is mainly a ceiling light plus daylight from a window off to the left, which leaves the right side of his face a touch shadowed. He has a broad, weathered face with light stubber growth, short greying brown hair cut close at the sides and receding at the temples, and a neutral expression with a faint polite half-smile. No glasses. He wears a navy quarter-zip fleece over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall in a small spare-room office with a white IKEA bookshelf holding ring binders, a few engineering reference books, a framed photo of a teenage girl, and a small Springboks mug used as a pen pot. A road bike helmet hangs on a hook near the door frame at the edge of the image.
